name: Speculation Rules (prefetch and prerender)
plain: A page can tell the browser to load and render the next page in the background.
meaning: A site can preload other URLs the person may visit. Prerendered pages run scripts before the person arrives, so analytics and counters may fire on a visit that never happens.

access.persistence: While the page is open; discarded when not used
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Same-site prerender by default; cross-origin prefetch needs opt-in
steps: Browser fetches or prerenders per eagerness

limits.headline: Can tell your browser to load the likely next page before you tap
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you hover over or get close to a link.
can: Load the next page in the background before you tap it
Show the next page right away when you do tap
Pick pages to preload on its own site
cannot: Preload pages when your browser has data saver or low power on
Run the other page's sign in or purchase actions
Preload pages from other sites with your logged in details
limits.reach_label: Only its own likely next pages
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge and Safari support it. Firefox does not yet.

story.what_it_is: A page can tell the browser to load the next page before you click it.

marketing.name: Prerender pages in Chrome
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say prerendering the likely next page can make navigation feel instant.

story.for_you: The next page appears almost instantly when you click. What you do not see is that your browser may have loaded it for you earlier, even if you never opened it.
story.for_makers: Makers bet on where you will click next and load it early to boost speed, which lifts search ranking and sales. The cost is extra data use and the site may count visits you never made.

use_cases.example: On a store listing, the top product page is loaded in the background so tapping it feels instant.
A news site prerenders the next top story from the home page.
A streaming service prefetches the title page of a show you are hovering over.
Analytics must avoid counting prerendered pages that the person never actually viewed.
An ad system waits to count an impression until a prerendered page is really shown.
A booking site prerenders the next step of search results.

technical_bounds: Chrome limits: eagerness immediate or eager up to 50 prefetches and 10 prerenders; moderate or conservative up to 2 (FIFO)
Disabled when Data Saver or Energy Saver is on, when Preload pages is off, or memory is low
Prerendered pages defer permission prompts, notifications, geolocation and other sensitive APIs until activation
Cross-origin prerender is not allowed; same-site cross-origin prefetch needs opt in
Support per MDN BCD: Chrome and Edge 109, Safari 27.3; Firefox has not shipped it

abuse: Loading pages to disclose IP or cookies before click

history.change: Prefetch and prerender via speculation rules
